content: Aluminium acetotartrate, also known as ALSOL, is an organic compound that functions as an astringent and disinfectant. It is the aluminium salt derived from acetic acid and tartaric acid. This compound appears as colorless or slightly yellowish crystals. It is freely soluble in water, although the dissolution process is exceedingly slow. It is insoluble in alcohol and ether. In medical applications, aluminium acetotartrate is utilized in various concentrations for specific purposes. A 0.5–2% solution is used as a nasal douche to manage conditions affecting the respiratory tract. A 1–3% solution serves as a substitute for aluminium acetate solution. In more concentrated forms, it is applied as a lotion to treat frostbite and balanitis. Additionally, it is combined with boric acid and used as a snuff for the treatment of atrophic rhinitis. Aluminium acetotartrate is also incorporated into antiseptic vulnerary ointments and creams for wound care.
